To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a new method for OD and OC segmentation in fundus photographs that outperforms the state-of-the- art on two datasets, and that we generalise our approach to segment four datasets, outperforming or achieving comparable results to the state-of-the art on all four datasets.
we propose a new method to segment the optic disc and cup in fundus images using deep-learning.
we have developed and validated a novel deep learning-based method for OD and OC segmentation, and demonstrated that the method generalizes across fundus devices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the automatic delineation of OD features for early glaucoma detection.
the automatic segmentation of the OD and OC from retinal fundus images for glaucoma detection and diagnosis.
the development of a deep-learning-based method for automatic delineation of the OC and OD in colour fundus images, which can be used to estimate the cup-to-disc ratio for early glaucoma diagnosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method can be used to segment OD and OC boundaries from fundus images with high accuracy, and can be used for glaucoma management.
the proposed method can accurately segment the OD and OC in fundus images, which can be used to estimate the glaucoma CDR.
the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the art on four datasets from different devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods on four different datasets and is able to generalise to unseen datasets without further training.
we present a new deep-learning method for OD segmentation, which is able to generalise to different datasets without any retraining.

the proposed method is able to generalise well to different datasets, which is crucial to the adoption of automatic glaucoma diagnosis in the clinic.
